newsitem.title: UK: BP Grangemouth refinery restarting after power cut.
newsitem.headline: BP Grangemouth refinery restarting after power cut.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc said on Tuesday that its 180,000 barrel per day (bpd) Scottish Grangemouth refinery was restarting operations after a power failure closed the plant on Monday afternoon.
The neighbouring Kinneil separation plant, which handles production from Britain's biggest oilfield system Forties, was also being returned to service, a BP spokesman said.
Grangemouth and Kinneil were shut down in a controlled operation at 1730 GMT on Monday after the loss of power to the entire complex, the spokesman said.
Power resumed at 2100 GMT and operations got underway to restart the refinery shortly afterwards.
Some refinery units were not expected back to full service for a day or more.
Kinneil, which handles some 950,000 bpd of Forties crude throughput, was running partially on Tuesday morning.
It was not immediately clear whether there was any impact on Forties production.
